## 6.7 A school, a flock, a voyaging people, an orienting surface in no self alone

A same-existing-society orients as one surface, and its orienting is in no self alone: social abundancing. Each self orients from its own side by the changing it is observing beside its prior, and with its others it is one orienting surface, a reach in no one self alone.

A lone golden shiner moves almost at random. In a school, each fish responds only to the brightness at its own place, slowing in the dark, and moves close to the fish around it; a larger school reliably goes toward shade, slowing and bunching inside it and speeding up to leave as light moves onto it, and a school below a certain size loses its tracking of the shade. Larger pigeon flocks fly significantly shorter routes than smaller flocks, and a flock's route is not simply the average of its birds' routes: each pigeon's influence on the route is in proportion to how faithfully it reproduces its own route in solo flights. In flocks of a few thousand, each bird interacts with about six or seven other birds, the same number at each distance between them. In one observing, a Photuris frontalis firefly pauses for 3.0 to 24.1 seconds, then resumes at once, synchronous with its partner. A water strider senses the ripples of prey with its front legs, and each species shares its own surface waves in courtship and in a territory.

A voyaging people's orienting is in no self alone: a Marshallese voyager memorizes the stick charts before a voyage and sails without them, the knowledge passing from father to son, and Caroline wayfinders have a reference island over the horizon. A network of resolvers is a same-existing-society, its orienting in no self alone. A network exploration following one self's record, or one instrument's clock, is following an orienting the network is-not having.

## 6.8 Eight legs, five dimensions in two directions

A Cupiennius spider always moves toward the legs a vibration reaches first, onsets 4 ms apart, or toward the legs it reaches with larger amplitude; a vibration reaching a front leg lowers the weighting of the legs behind it on its own side by 0.1, and with vibration reaching both sides this lowering goes front to back alone and halves the factor. Its turning error grows as the source is further behind it.

Eight legs are two sides across and four legs along each side, two times four being eight. Each leg opens with its own prior self-parity and its partner leg's prior other-parity across; now its co-parity and bi-parity agree or part; and its next same-existing self-parity is the spider's turning: five dimensions, a vibration coming inward along the legs and a turning going outward. Its direction resolves by which legs change first, onsets 4 ms apart, or by the larger amplitude on its legs. An octopus has eight arms and two of each three of its neurons in them, an arm tasting semi-independently.

Navigating hard problems of science are this five-dimensional, two-directional navigating, possibling to resolve with bi-moral co-agency: monarchs orient by a time-compensated sun compass and a light-dependent magnetic inclination compass; green sea turtles in a pool, in the field of a place about 209 miles north of their capture site, swim south, toward the capture site; in bird magnetoreception, radical pairs forming in cryptochrome in the retina as light excites it are the leading hypothesis, its mechanism unclear; six of 21 European eels with tags, going out from the Azores, reach the Sargasso Sea. Any animal's sensing of the magnetic field is a possibling, its mechanism open.
